personalIntro.p1: I’m Ernso Azor, a brand designer and strategist based in Curitiba, Brazil, with 8+ years spent working across institutions, professionals, and creatives who refuse to be average. I help people and companies uncover what actually makes them different, then build an identity that puts it on full display. Not decoration. Not guesswork. I look for the truth that’s already sitting inside a brand, the part its owner usually can’t see because they’re too close to it, and I give it a shape the world can’t ignore.
personalIntro.p2: I’m on a mission to work with ambitious institutions, driven professionals, and bold creatives ready to be seen at the level they actually operate, not the one their current presence suggests.
personalIntro.p3: Whether you’re a corporation ready to lead with the authority you’ve already earned, or an artist ready to be felt before you’re heard, I bring the same discipline: strategy first, storytelling that makes people look twice, and craft that makes sure they remember you.

worlds.title: The worlds I operate in.
worlds.world1Body: For institutions that operate at scale and need a brand presence as strong as the work they do. Strategic identity systems that command credibility in boardrooms, with partners, and in public, before a single word is spoken.
worlds.world2Body: For driven professionals who have built real expertise and now need the world to see it clearly. A personal brand that positions them at the level they actually operate, not the one their current presence suggests.
worlds.world3Body: For artists, influencers, and public figures who move audiences but haven't yet built the brand architecture to match their talent. Full brand identity, social positioning, and a system that makes their presence as powerful as their work.

about.metaDescription: Brand strategist & designer. 8+ years across three worlds. The thread that holds.

parcours.p1: It started long before I had a word for any of it. As a child, I was the one who noticed things nobody else seemed to register: the way a logo felt subtly wrong even when I couldn’t say why, the way a single colour could change the entire mood of a room, the way some names lodged themselves in your memory forever while others vanished the moment you looked away. I wasn’t studying identity. I was simply unable to stop seeing it, in everything, all the time. That kind of attention doesn’t feel like a gift when you’re young. It feels like noise. It took years to understand it was actually a compass.
parcours.p2: That compass finally found its language in 2018, in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at one of the country’s leading technical schools, where I enrolled to train as a computer science technician, not a designer. Graphic design entered my life almost as an afterthought, a single module tucked inside a much larger technical curriculum. But the moment I touched it, everything the child in me had been noticing for years suddenly had somewhere to go. I wasn’t learning a new skill. I was finally being handed the vocabulary for something I’d already been doing instinctively my whole life.
parcours.p3: The real turning point came fast, faster than I was ready for. In my second year, still a student with more theory than experience, a company trusted me to build its entire visual identity from nothing. I remember the weight of that moment more than the details of the brief: the realization that someone was staking their business, their name, their credibility, on my judgment. I said yes anyway. That project became the proof I’ve carried ever since: precision isn’t just a technical habit, it’s a form of respect. The same rigor that makes a system run without failure is the exact rigor that makes a brand impossible to look away from.
parcours.p4: Today, that dual foundation, an engineer’s obsession with structure and a designer’s instinct for what moves people, shows up in every project I touch, whether the client is a corporation, a founder, or an artist. Strategy always comes before style. Nothing is decorative unless it’s also deliberate. And every identity I build still starts exactly where it started for me at nineteen: with the discipline to notice what’s actually true, and the craft to make sure no one can ignore it again.

drives.p1: I don’t do this for the applause. I do it because most people, and most brands, are walking around with their real value hidden in plain sight, and that feels like a waste I can’t ignore.
drives.p2: Every project starts the same way: not with a mood board, but with a question. What is actually true here, that hasn’t been said yet? Corporation, professional, or artist, it doesn’t matter. The moment someone stops managing how they’re perceived and starts building from what’s real, everything changes: how they’re trusted, how they’re remembered, how they’re paid.
drives.p3: That’s the job. Not to make things look good. To make the truth impossible to miss.

beyond.p1: Outside brand strategy, I’m still building. I run my own digital ventures, and digital marketing is as much an obsession as design: understanding how attention moves, what makes someone stop scrolling and actually stay, never really leaves me.
beyond.p2: The rest of my life follows the same instinct that runs through my work: notice, refine, repeat. I play guitar. I train, because discipline in the gym and discipline in a brand system come from the same place. I spend hours in tutorials and podcasts from people who think sharper than I do, not to collect information, but because learning never stops feeling urgent to me.
beyond.p3: I’m drawn to nature for the same reason I’m drawn to identity: it rewards attention. Look closely enough at anything and it starts telling you the truth about itself.
beyond.p4: I hold myself to a standard most people would call excessive. Everything I touch, a project, a room, a plan, has to be right, not almost right. And I do my best thinking alone. Solitude isn’t withdrawal for me, it’s where I actually interrogate myself and question my own decisions before anyone else has to. It’s how ambition stays honest instead of becoming noise.
beyond.p5: I think in decades, not quarters.

beliefs.title: Branding is revelation
beliefs.body: A brand is never invented. It is uncovered. The most powerful identities feel inevitable — like they could only belong to that person, that institution, that artist. My job is to make that truth visible.

beliefs.title: Uniqueness is the strategy
beliefs.body: In a world of imitation, the most dangerous thing a brand can do is look like someone else. What makes you different — whether you're a CEO or a creator — is not a risk. It is your greatest asset.

beliefs.title: Perception is power
beliefs.body: How the world sees you determines what comes to you. For a corporation, it shapes deals. For an expert, it shapes authority. For an artist, it shapes reach. Managing perception is not vanity — it is strategy.

beliefs.title: Design is a philosophy
beliefs.body: Every color, typeface, and spatial decision communicates something. There are no neutral choices. Everything means something — which means everything must be intentional, from a boardroom annual report to an Instagram grid.

beliefs.title: Alignment is the goal
beliefs.body: A brand works when what you say, what you show, and what you do all point in the same direction — whether on a company website or a creator's social presence. Misalignment is the most expensive mistake a brand can make.

beliefs.title: The REVEAL Framework
beliefs.body: Root → Excavate → Voice → Express → Align → Launch. A proprietary six-stage methodology that works across all three worlds: finding and revealing the authentic identity that was always there, waiting to be seen.

privacy.s1Body1: The only personal information this site collects is what you choose to submit through the Initiate contact form: your name, email address, brand or product name, estimated timeline and budget, how you found me, and a description of your project. If you email or message me directly instead, I receive whatever information you include in that message.
privacy.s1Body2: This site does not use cookies, analytics, or advertising trackers. No account creation, payment information, or browsing behaviour is collected at any point.
